subject: Eastus3 service continuity advisory — rolling node restarts & driver refresh
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Eastus3 service continuity advisory — rolling node restarts & driver refresh

Hi Jordan and Acme ops team,

Heads up: we have a planned maintenance operation in the Eastus3 region on Friday, 2028-06-18. Scope: rolling restarts across a subset of inference node fleets to apply a kernel/driver security and performance update (driver 5.1.3 -> 5.2.0, kernel ABI compat fixes).

Why: the driver update fixes an intermittent NVLink regression and improves GPU driver memory handling under sustained KV-cache loads. We've validated the update on staging and limited canaries; we are now scheduling production rollout.

Planned window (proposed):
- Start: 2028-06-18 01:00 UTC (06:00 PDT)
- End: 2028-06-18 07:00 UTC (00:00 PDT)
- Impact: rolling restarts of small node batches; expected transient connection resets for in-flight requests (sub-1s token latency blips). No data plane changes; models and keys remain intact.

Mitigations in place:
- Continuous small-batch rotations to limit blast radius
- Automated fallback routing to healthy availability zones if a node fails health checks
- KV-prefix cache warmers for high-QPS customers during handoffs
- Extra on-call SRE coverage and a dedicated remediation channel (see link below)

Attachments: eastus3-maintenance-runbook.pdf (runbook + rollback steps).

Request: please let us know if the proposed window conflicts with any scheduled heavy inference workloads on your side. If you prefer a different start time, indicate preferred windows and we will try to accommodate.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Site Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference platform
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eastus3 service continuity advisory — rolling node restarts & driver refresh

Thanks for the heads up, Sean. A couple quick clarifying questions:

1) Our highest throughput window is 2028-06-18 19:00-21:00 UTC (spike in batch scoring). The proposed window looks fine for the morning, but can you confirm you won't be doing any follow-up operations later in the day?
2) If a node fails health checks during the update, what's the expected time to failover to a healthy node in another AZ? We need to communicate any possible amplification to our support teams.

Also, please avoid kickoff between 15:00-16:00 PDT if possible — that's when our internal batch job pushes heavy traffic.

Jordan
Ops Lead, Acme AI
jordan.lee@acme.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 12:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eastus3 service continuity advisory — rolling node restarts & driver refresh

Jordan — thanks for the fast reply and good context. Internal notes for coordination:

- We can shift the active rotation window earlier by two hours to avoid the 15:00-16:00 PDT conflict Jordan mentioned. Proposed new window: 2028-06-18 23:00-05:00 UTC (16:00-22:00 PDT). Sean, Irene — is that workable given our canary health progression?
- Failover: automated routing typically completes within 30-90s for our infra (most customers see <2s interruption), but in a worst-case driver panic we may require node evacuation and replacement (10-20 minutes). We will keep Acme notified via the remediation channel and update the status page.
- Action items: I will update the runbook timing and create a mutual action plan doc. Sean, please attach the postmortem-template.docx so customer-facing PMs have the follow-up format.

Jordan — once we confirm the moved window is OK on your side we'll lock it and send a final advisory 24 hours before the operation.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

> On Thu, 14 Jun 2028 at 09:12, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Heads up: we have a planned maintenance operation in the Eastus3 region on Friday, 2028-06-18. Scope: rolling restarts across a subset of inference node fleets to apply a kernel/driver security and performance update...
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Eastus3 service continuity advisory — rolling node restarts & driver refresh

Jordan — thanks, we appreciate the heads-up about your traffic pattern. We updated the schedule per Marissa's note. Finalized window: 2028-06-18 23:00 UTC — 2028-06-19 05:00 UTC (16:00-22:00 PDT).

What to expect:
- We'll perform staggered restarts in 15–20 minute batches so any single model serving surface will only see sub-second reconnects while routing rehydrates.
- Our runbook (attached) includes explicit rollback triggers: repeated health-check failures across 3 consecutive batches -> immediate halt and automatic rollback to prior driver.
- If you see any unexpected behavior please open a ticket to ops@redwood.com and ping #remediation-eastus3 for immediate SRE attention. We'll also publish incremental updates on status.redwood.com/eastus3.

Attachments: eastus3-maintenance-runbook.pdf, postmortem-template.docx.

After the operation we will:
- Circulate a summary email within 24 hours outlining any customer-visible events and remediation actions.
- Publish a short postmortem if we observe any deviation from expected behavior.

Thanks again for the quick feedback — we're locking the new time.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Site Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
